rules: Blocked legacy surface identities must not be exposed as public navigation destinations.
Legacy files and URLs may remain reachable only for migration compatibility and must not be advertised by the new shell.
Visible words such as about or video are not globally forbidden when they are ordinary content labels; the gate targets legacy surface identity/destination semantics.
LivingWaterWest must express institutional information inside its own information architecture rather than linking to the retired global About surface.
New framework code must not introduce links to /content/website or equivalent retired catch-all destinations.
Physical deletion remains blocked until the legacy retirement deletion gate is satisfied.
